chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Halbi, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a house that had not been partitioned, so one of the people of the house gave in charity his share from the house. He said: 'It is permissible.' I said, 'What is your view if it was a gift?' He said: 'It is permissible.'

He said, 'And I asked him about a man who settled another man in his house for his lifetime. He said: 'It is permissible for him, and it is not for him to evict him.' I said, 'So it is for him and his offspring.' He said: 'It is permissible.'
And I asked him about a man who settled another man but did not stipulate any specific time for him. He said: 'The owner of the house may evict him if he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic legal rulings on gifting or donating a share of an undivided property and granting lifetime tenancy?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the validity of disposing of undivided property shares through charity or gift, reflecting the Shia juristic view that individual co-owners possess independent authority over their specific portions. It further delineates the rights in lifetime tenancy (i'jar), distinguishing between irrevocable grants for life (and potentially heirs) and indefinite tenancies where the owner retains the right to evict at will, underscoring the flexibility of private property rights in Islamic law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ahmad Bin Umar Al Halby, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a house which was not distributed, so one of the people of the house gave in charity with his share from the house. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is allowed’. I said, ‘What is your<sup>asws</sup> view if he had gifted it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is allowed’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who settled a man in his house for his lifetime. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is allowed, and it is not for him that he should throw him out’. I said, ‘So it is for him and his offspring’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is allowed’.

And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who settles a man but does not stipulate anything from the time period for him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The owner of the house can vacate him if he so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 24. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Ahmad ibn ‘Umar al-Halabiy from his father who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a house which is not yet distributed and a certain one of the people of the house gives his share as charity. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if it is a grant?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible.’

I then asked him (the Imam) about a man who allows another man to use his house for his lifetime. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible but he cannot evict him.’ I then asked, ‘Can it be for him and those whom he leaves behind?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is permissible.’

I then asked about the case in which one gives permission to another person to use a house without the mention of time duration. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can ask him to leave if he wants him to vacate the house.’”
